quote_misfit_classes.method: For each of the 22 rows the skill.json row was located, its quote resolved against every cited record via kb text, and the cited record printed in full. Class (a) = the quote (or the flagged co-cited record) does support the row's assertion and the scanner is wrong. Class (b) = the quote is a verbatim substring but the row's post-marker clause states a domain fact the record does not contain, so that clause should be split out and marked proposed. Class (c) = the cited record does not bear on any clause of the row.

mechanical_check.proposal: A two-limb rule in tools/validate_skills.py, applied to every origin=sourced row. Limb 1 (anchor-per-citation): today the validator accepts a row when the quote is a substring of ANY cited record (`any(q in KB_TEXT[x] for x in srcs)`, validate_skills.py:161). Change the schema so a row carries one quote per cited id and flag any cited id no recorded quote anchors. Limb 2 (restate-and-extend): flag a sourced row whose text matches /already states?|what it adds|what \w[\w-]* adds/i and does not contain the word 'proposed' - this repo's convention is 'X already states F-nnn. What it adds here: ...', and the clause after the marker is the author's own extension, which must carry either its own quote or origin=proposed. Neither limb judges meaning: limb 1 is substring containment, limb 2 is a regex plus a keyword.
mechanical_check.hit_rate_on_b_and_c: 5/5 (limb 2 catches 4/4 of class b; limb 1 catches 1/1 of class c)
mechanical_check.rejected_alternative: A lexical-novelty score (fraction of the row's content words absent from every cited record and from the quote) does not separate the classes: the 22 misfits score 0.53-1.00 while the repo-wide median over 1413 sourced rows is 0.80 and the quartiles are 0.67/0.88. The class (b) rows sit at 0.75-1.00, inside the bulk of correct rows. Measured and discarded.
mechanical_check.recommendation_detail: Adopt limb 2 now as a validator WARNING: it catches every class (b) row, fires on 2/22 random correct rows and on 204/1413 repo-wide, which is a reviewable backlog, and its remedy is mechanical (split the post-marker clause into its own row with origin=proposed, or give it its own quote). Adopt limb 1 as a SCHEMA change rather than a warning: as a check it fires on 43% of rows and 8/22 correct ones, which is unusable as a gate, but as an authoring requirement (one quote per id) it makes the 608 unanchored citations impossible to write in the first place and it is the only limb that catches class (c). Neither limb decides whether a supported row is truly supported: 17 of the 22 flagged rows were sound, so a sampled human or independent-model review of sourced rows remains the mitigation for semantics, and the two limbs only narrow what that review has to look at.

The one product name in the example (examples/end-to-end/run.py:165) is inside class OpenAICompatibleAdapter and the docstring de-pins it. The load path is data, not prose: every skill declares composes_with.builds_on/used_by, validate_skills.py:452-468 errors on an unknown target, on an asymmetric link in either direction, and on any divergence from docs/skill-manifest.json; manifest_facets.py check() additionally errors on a builds_on whose wave is not strictly lower. 101 skills, 0 errors. docs/skill-graph.md is generated from the skill.json files rather than hand-written, and 0 builds_on edges are dangling, so the published graph is complete. T2.2 is enforced concretely by the 'compose by name, not by copy' warning keyed on (kb id, verbatim quote) - the 35 open warnings are the residue of that rule, not a failure of it.

The consumption contract exists and runs: cap-consumption states one shape for all four entries, examples/end-to-end/entries/ holds human.json, event.json, schedule.json and external.json, and `bash examples/end-to-end/test.sh` gives 'passed 29, failed 0' including 'nothing written for an invalid envelope' and 'final chain verifies'. Both scanner breakages were caught with typed problem details. Against T3.2 ('cannot be daunting'), the surface is heavy: 101 skills, 2.45 MB of SKILL.md, and a README whose own counts are stale in three places (QH-001/002/005) - the first thing a newcomer reads currently misstates the layer count and the ledger size, which is the cheapest possible loss of trust.

Sourcing is enforced, not asserted: 1507 sourced rows each carry a quote the validator proves is a verbatim substring of a cited record, and the knowledge base is hash-chained - `kb.py verify` reports 'chains intact, source hash matches, every fact matches its lines, rebuild is identical'. Gaps are listed rather than invented: blueprint_check reports '204 entries, 171 sourced, 40 gaps, 23 listed gaps, 0 errors' and errors on a status:gap entry missing from gaps[]. The honesty is load-bearing in both directions - run-summary's known_defects itself records that 49% of rows are proposed, that all 541 research records are search-only with no verified page fetch, and that every ceremony reviewer was 'sonnet'. My own audit of the 22 flagged rows found 5 real defects (4 over-extensions, 1 irrelevant citation), a ~2.3% defect rate on the 214 sampled sourced rows.

The loop closes into the checker, which is the test T4.4 actually implies. validate_skills.py's docstring lists rules that exist because a ceremony found the defect: 'ceremony 10, C10-001' (an -implement breakage that copies its ideal's), 'ceremony 9, C9-001' (a minted adapter entity id), and author-brief defect items 2, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14 - each a warning added after a review, not before. Findings per skill fall across the run: 1.00, 1.00, 0.38, 0.07, 0.07, 0.07, 0.14, 0.00, 0.12, 0.00 for ceremonies 1-10, over sections that grew from 4 to 15 skills. 26 ceremony records under kb/ceremonies/, 62 findings applied and 7 declined with reasons. The weakness is the grader: run-summary's known_defects admits every reviewer was the same model family, which is why this outside verification pass found 5 real quote defects and 1 tool that cannot run at all.

summary: Of 15 scanner findings I confirmed 9, downgraded 4 and refuted 2, and found one the scanners missed: tools/gaps.py crashes on the repo's own research data and cannot run at all, which is the only true block left. The 22 quote-misfit rows are mostly scanner error - 17 are properly supported, 4 over-extend a citation into a claim the record does not make (all four use the 'X already states F-nnn. What it adds here' pattern), and 1 cites a record that bears on nothing in the row - so the real defect rate on sampled sourced rows is about 2.3%, and a two-limb mechanical rule (one quote per cited id, plus a regex on the restate-and-extend marker) catches all 5 at 18/22 recall and 8/22 false positives, which is worth adopting as a warning and a schema change but not as a gate. On direction the framework is loose, composable and sourced on evidence I reproduced, self-improving in the way that matters most (four validator rules exist because a ceremony found the defect), and only partly usable: the code path works end to end at 29/29, but the README a newcomer reads first misstates three of its own counts.
